method: Direct inspection of 10 production PNGs across all five real sources and synthetic/segmented cases, plus two supplementary detail views.

figures.notes: Full real move-head source: Before extends to raw end; After trim at 58 s is dotted in TD/After STFT; signal/spectral panels render correctly.
Real talk Ch2: TD/STFT display to 60 elapsed s, PSD retains full-segment definition; labels and paired color scale readable.
Real vibration level1 Ch1: consistent channel labels, elapsed display and independently verified PSD/STFT values.
Real vibration level2 Ch2: transient amplitude preserved in the view; spectral panels readable without interpreting numerical agreement as signal quality.
Real vibration level3 Ch1: full 60-second display, no layout clipping; PSD and STFT panels readable.
Real-signal segmented copy: separate S1/S2 Welch curves, TD breaks, STFT gaps blank; After tail at 12–13.006 s dotted; excluded tail hatched.
Source Ch3 is Before only. After panel explicitly states no model output; no old clamp to model Ch2 is drawn.
Synthetic nonzero epoch: elapsed starts at zero; Before retains 5.01-second coverage while After stops at 4 s, with dotted tail.
Half-second display: TD and full-source PSD remain visible; both STFT panels explicitly omitted because the displayed sample count does not exceed overlap 128.
Large integer epoch: retained spans near 10–14 s and excluded tail visible; tiny boundary requires detail view and numerical clipping tests.
Supplementary viewport: TD breaks between model centers 11.995 and 12.002 s; both STFTs blank from source end 11.996 to 12.002 s. No spectrum/method changes.
Supplementary viewport: excluded first 20 ms is hatched, following missing span blank; PSD unchanged from production plot.

limitations: Subpixel spans require numerical source/clip checks and supplementary zooms; overview pixels alone cannot verify six-ms gaps.
Supplementary renderer intersects source clips with its narrower viewport; no CLI zoom option is introduced.
Signal quality remains disabled; numerical equivalence is not a quality assessment.
